Works.....now - This unit is OK I guess for the money. The 1st time I used it, it made ice & filled the bin & shut down & never came back on. I tried a couple of things from the rather sparse troubleshooting guide to no avail. As a last ditch effort I plugged it back in one morning & at work, applied to return it. When I got home that evening, the bin was full of ice and it's worked fine ever since.
Apparently the mere threat of returning it to China was enough to get it to do what it was supposed to.
It is VERY noisey and mine appears to have a rattle somewhere near the fan. If I rap the side of it near the fan it stops for a few moments but then starts again.
The ice it produces is very porous and melts very quickly in a drink...which is OK since I just use it for water but in mixed drinks and soda, etc, it would water it down very quickly. You can put some of the ice into baggies & put in your freezer to harden but that's why I bought this unit...I didn't want to take up space in my small apartment-sized fridge to make and store ice.
The way the system is designed, the unit doesn't hold the ice below freezing so after dumping into the bin, it begins to melt. The water from melting goes back into the water supply tank and is used again to make ice over and over. I strongly recommend using filtered water like a Brita pitcher to fill the tank. The ice produced will not have a taste to it like using tap water. The water in the tank will also last longer. The instructions recommend draining the water from the tank every day. That would be a total pain and using filtered water I just do it about once a week or every few days if I'm not using a lot of ice.
Bottom line, if you're wanting an ice maker to use behind your home wet bar, keep looking and spend the money for a higher quality unit. If you just want some ice in your water, this unit is OK for that.

Great way to bring a washing machine back to life - Something got sloshed over the top of the tub in our washing machine and got down in the pump and chewed it up. I knew the pump was stuck because I could hear a very slight humming sound when it tried to drain the tub. I ordered this, watched a few videos on YouTube about how to replace it...and...now I have a working washing machine again for a lot less than a repair man would charge me just to drive to the house and tell me what the problem was.

Tips:

It just works - The design by the dishwasher manufacturer makes this part susceptible to breaking because the end with the single hole / eyelet attaches to a bolt head, and the cable bends about 90 degrees to where it goes over the plastic / nylon pulley wheel. That pulley wheel has no groove for the cable, and I am surprised it has lasted all these years.

Starting the job requires removing several screws holding the two bottom cover panels - two screws on each end in my application. Then you have access to the broken cable. It's unlikely that both cables would break at the same time since one will break causing the springs to let go - and the door will be heavy.

The 2 springs that support most of the weight of the door are attached to the other end that has 2 holes. Two cables are required, and both probably should be replaced at the same time.

Once those springs are attached to the cables, the eyelet ends can be slipped over the bolt heads. The first is simple to attach, but it has to have some tension on it so it does not slip off the pulley wheel while attaching the other end. Stretching the springs is best done using some tool - maybe a locking pliers - and wearing leather work gloves to prevent hurting your hands when it slips. That is the hardest part of this procedure ... more than standing on your head to replace the screws when reattaching the two bottom cover panels.

This is the part that has been breaking about every 5 years on my model dishwasher. At 29 years of age, the dishwasher may be replaced the next time this cable breaks. Hopefully the next model will be designed better and won't require this continued replacement.

It's small but powerful. - I've had it three days now and done several loads. As everyone else said, the hose will not fit a sink in the US. For the first day, I used bowls to fill the machine which was a lot of work but did the job. The next day, I bought a funnel big enough to cover my shower head, drilled two holes on opposite sides at the top, and used a small bungie cord to put a hook into each hole and then hang it over the shower head. I then cut two slits into the hose to allow the funnel to fit inside the faucet end, then duct taped it to seal. I attached the hose to the machine and it worked perfectly. My shower is low flow so I could turn it on full. I put the machine in the shower and ran it from there with no issues, other than to hold the machine when the spinner starts up because the vibration is very strong. My overall reaction is that it does a good job cleaning and the spinner is very good. Similar to a spa's machine to dry your bathing suit. It is labor intensive because you must move the clothes a few at a time to the spinner and you can only put a few things in at a time, but my clothes dry beautifully on a rack and the towels only need 15 minutes in a dryer at the laundromat until I can string up a clothesline in the summer. Excellent medium-sized refrigerator. - I bought my LG LTCS20020W top-freezer refrigerator from a local Lowes, so you won't see an Amazon purchase notice. Shrug. I've only owned it for a short while, but here's the skinny:

FREEZER:

The top freezer hits the ideal 0 degrees F in just a few hours by setting the thermostat on the center position. I deliberately bought a unit with no ice maker on the theory that ice makers are notorious troublemakers. DOWNSIDE: there's NO FREEZER LIGHT. I stuck a little Motion Sensor LED Night Light to the freezer roof to fix the issue.

REFRIGERATOR:

The refrigerator achieved 37-40 degrees F in a few hours with the thermostat only on the second position. My fridge is a simple unit with LED light, two crisper drawers, a smallish dairy bin and two shelves. Some units include an optional door alarm and pantry drawer, but not mine.

OVERALL:

This LG top-freezer refrigerator is VERY quiet and energy efficient. The dimensions are excellent for my small kitchen and contains enough food for over a week for my wife and I. This refrigerator is just a tiny bit shorter and narrower than some, which can be a major plus when situating it in some kitchens, especially in older houses. But the refrigerator is an inch or two deeper than some, so measure carefully.

I didn't realize it at first, but the doors are reversible. The fridge comes set up with the doors opening to the right, but even an inexperienced person (like myself) can switch the hardware so the doors open to the left in an hour by following the on-line videos.

LG refrigerators have a some of the best reputations for reliability, so I'm expecting this LG LTCS20020 to outlast me. Five stars.
